Pre-state warfare: loose formations broke early. Educated guess.

dailyRecovery.note: Morale (0..1) regained per day out of contact. Clark (1954): battalions forced from attack to defense needed 'a few days of recuperation and reinforcement'; those that reorganized did so in 4-24 h. Recovering ~0.3 of morale in 3-7 days -> 0.04-0.10/day; mid 0.07.

supplyShortfallPenalty.note: Morale lost per day at a total supply shortfall. Educated guess.

defeatShock.note: Morale drop on losing a battle. Educated guess.

capitalLossShock.note: Morale drop on losing the capital: Paris 1814 and 1871 ended resistance, Moscow 1812 did not; wide range. Educated guess. UNSOURCED ENGINE-SCALE CONSTANT: it is a step on the engine's 0..1 morale scale, which no source measures. Evidence that would set it: a set of out-of-sample wars (not the 24 backtest battles) in which the capital fell while the field army was intact, with an observable on both sides of the date (daily surrender or desertion rate, or share of formations still fighting 30 days later), converted to the engine scale through the same observable at defeatShock (one lost battle). Without that conversion any number is a guess; left grade D, value not tuned toward any outcome.
